items.name: Toro Verde Adventure Park — 'The Beast' Zip Line
items.hours: Wed-Sun 8am-4pm (last entry 1pm); closed Mon-Tue. Reservation required.
items.admission_cost: $99-$135 per person depending on zip-line package
items.description: Home of 'The Monster' (formerly the longest zip line in the world at 2.5 km) and 'The Beast,' which has you flying superman-style at up to 95 mph over a verdant central-mountain valley. Multi-line packages, suspension bridge, and 'Pretty Monster' line for those wanting the view without the top-speed plunge.
items.why_it_matters: The single most extreme zip line experience in the Americas — nothing in the Caribbean or US comes close to the scale, speed, or scenery of Toro Verde's central cordillera setting.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 75-90 min drive SW via PR-22 and PR-10 to Orocovis — no public transit; rental car or shuttle required
items.accessibility_notes: Not wheelchair accessible. Weight limits: 70-275 lbs for The Beast/Monster. Minimum age 10 for most lines; harness fit required.
items.gear_needed: Closed-toe athletic shoes (mandatory), athletic clothing, hair tied back; harness and helmet provided

items.name: Carabalí Rainforest Park — ATV Rainforest Adventure
items.hours: Daily 9am-4pm; tours depart at 9am, 11am, 1pm, 3pm. Reservation required.
items.admission_cost: $95-$135 single rider / $160-$200 double rider for 1-2 hr tours
items.description: Single- or two-seat ATVs along muddy trails at the foothills of El Yunque on a 600-acre private ranch. Routes pass river crossings, jungle canopy, and a panoramic ocean overlook. Beginner instruction included before you set off behind a lead guide.
items.why_it_matters: The most popular family-friendly off-road experience near San Juan — combines El Yunque-edge rainforest scenery with adrenaline, without the long drives to remote operators.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 45-55 min drive E via PR-3 to Luquillo; many operators offer SJ hotel pickup as add-on
items.accessibility_notes: Not wheelchair accessible. Drivers must be 16+ with valid license; passengers 6+. Closed-toe shoes mandatory. Expect to get muddy.
items.gear_needed: Closed-toe shoes you don't mind ruining, change of clothes, sunglasses, bandana for dust; helmets and goggles provided

items.name: Carabalí Rainforest Park — Horseback Beach & Rainforest Ride
items.hours: Daily 9am-3pm; rides depart hourly with reservation. 1-hr rainforest and 2-hr beach options.
items.admission_cost: $65 (1 hr rainforest) / $99 (2 hr beach + rainforest combo)
items.description: Ride a Paso Fino — Puerto Rico's smooth-gaited heritage horse breed — along jungle trails or down to a stretch of secluded beach near Luquillo. The 2-hour combo loops through the rainforest and ends with a horseback walk in the surf.
items.why_it_matters: The only nearby ride where you can experience the smooth gait of an authentically Puerto Rican Paso Fino horse and dip your boots in the Atlantic in one outing.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 45-55 min drive E via PR-3 to Luquillo
items.accessibility_notes: Riders must be 6+ and under 240 lbs. Long pants and closed-toe shoes required. Not wheelchair accessible.
items.gear_needed: Long pants, closed-toe shoes (boots or sneakers), sunscreen, hat with chinstrap; helmets provided

items.name: Hacienda Campo Rico — ATV, Zip-Line & Horseback
items.hours: Daily 9am-4pm by reservation only; ATV at 9am/12pm/3pm, zip-line 10am/1pm.
items.description: A 2,200-acre former dairy estate 15 minutes from San Juan offers ATVs through mahogany groves, a 5-platform zip-line canopy tour, and gentle horseback rides. The closest 'big adventure' park to the metro area — perfect for travelers without a long-drive budget.
items.why_it_matters: By far the closest combined ATV/zip-line/horseback operator to Old San Juan — turns adventure activities into a half-day trip instead of a full-day commitment.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 20-25 min drive E via PR-26 to Carolina (Campo Rico exit)
items.accessibility_notes: Not wheelchair accessible. ATV drivers 16+ with license; zip-line minimum 70 lbs / max 250 lbs; horseback 8+.
items.gear_needed: Closed-toe shoes (mandatory), athletic clothing, sunscreen; helmets/harness provided

items.name: Río Camuy Cave Park (Parque de las Cavernas del Río Camuy)
items.hours: Wed-Sun 8:30am-3:30pm; closed Mon-Tue. Reservation strongly recommended.
items.description: Guided walking tour into Cueva Clara, a cathedral-sized chamber 170 ft tall, formed by the third-largest underground river in the world. A trolley shuttles you down into the sinkhole, then a paved path leads through stalactite formations with bilingual interpretation.
items.why_it_matters: The defining underground experience of Puerto Rico — the karst country here is one of the largest cave systems in the Western Hemisphere, and Cueva Clara is the most accessible chamber.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 90 min drive W via PR-22 to Camuy — a full-day commitment; pair with Arecibo or north-coast stops
items.accessibility_notes: Trolley + paved chamber path are mobility-friendly to a degree, but the cave entrance involves steep grades and stairs in places — confirm with park before visiting. Bring layers — cave is cooler than surface.
items.gear_needed: Closed-toe shoes with grip (cave floor is wet), light jacket, water, cash for parking and snacks

items.name: Cueva Ventana ('Window Cave')
items.description: A 45-minute guided walk through two limestone caves ending at a massive natural window opening with a panoramic view over the Río Grande de Arecibo valley. Bats overhead, Taíno petroglyphs near the entrance, and one of the most photographed views in Puerto Rico.
items.why_it_matters: The 'window' shot is the most iconic adventure-photo in Puerto Rico — and the cave itself is far shorter and easier than Camuy, making it doable as a half-day from San Juan.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 75 min drive W via PR-22 to Arecibo (PR-10 exit)
items.accessibility_notes: Not wheelchair accessible — uneven cave floor, low ceilings in spots, short scramble at the window. Bring a headlamp or phone flashlight as backup.
items.gear_needed: Closed-toe shoes with grip, water, insect repellent; helmets and flashlights provided by operator

items.name: Charco Azul (Patillas) — Natural Swimming Hole
items.hours: Daylight only (no formal hours); arrive before 10am on weekends to beat crowds.
items.admission_cost: Free; $5 informal parking on busy weekends
items.description: A short 0.5-mile rainforest walk leads to a crystalline mountain pool with a 15-ft cliff jump and a deep swimming basin fed by the Río Grande de Patillas. Locals come for the day with coolers; weekdays you may have it nearly to yourself.
items.why_it_matters: The most accessible cliff-jumping spot in Puerto Rico — a slice of mountain-river paradise that costs nothing and rewards travelers willing to drive to the southeast.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 75 min drive S via PR-52 and PR-184 to Patillas
items.accessibility_notes: No facilities — no bathrooms or lifeguards. Trail is uneven and can be slippery after rain. Jump at your own risk; check water depth first.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit, water shoes (mandatory — rocks are slippery), towel, packed lunch, trash bag (pack it out)

items.name: Las Tinajas / Charco Frío — Fajardo Hike & Swim
items.hours: Daylight; informal — no gate or hours. Best weekday mornings.
items.description: A 1-mile semi-technical hike along a stream in the Sierra de Luquillo leads to a chain of natural pools and small waterfalls. The largest, Charco Frío, has 8-12 ft jumps and a rope swing. The trail involves rock-hopping and a couple of waist-deep crossings.
items.why_it_matters: The east coast's best wild-swim hike — far less crowded than El Yunque's official waterfalls and free of the timed-entry pass system.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 55 min drive E via PR-3 to Fajardo (trailhead on PR-9990)
items.accessibility_notes: Not accessible — trail crosses streams and involves climbing over wet rocks. Skip after heavy rain (flash-flood risk). No facilities.
items.gear_needed: Water shoes or hiking sandals (mandatory), swimsuit, dry bag, snacks, headlamp if hiking out near sunset

items.name: Jet Ski Tour — Condado Lagoon & Coast
items.admission_cost: $110-$150 per jet ski (1 hr) / $180-$250 (2 hr); 2 riders per ski
items.description: Launch from Condado Lagoon and ride out along the protected lagoon and onto the Atlantic coastline with a hotel-skyline backdrop, escorted by a guide on a follow-along ski. Quick instructional briefing first; no boating license required.
items.why_it_matters: The fastest adrenaline hit reachable on foot from most San Juan hotels — no driving, no full-day commitment, and that postcard view of the Condado strip from the water.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 10 min Uber to Condado Lagoon (Laguna del Condado)
items.accessibility_notes: Drivers must be 16+ with photo ID; minimum age 5 to ride as passenger with adult. Closed-water swimmers recommended. Not wheelchair accessible.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit, reef-safe sunscreen, sunglasses with strap, GoPro mount optional; PFDs provided

items.name: Catamaran Day Trip to Icacos & La Cordillera Cays — Fajardo
items.hours: Daily departures 9am or 10am, return 4-5pm; check-in 30 min before. Reservation required.
items.admission_cost: $110-$160 per adult (includes lunch, drinks, gear) / $80-$100 child
items.description: Sail from Puerto del Rey marina out to the uninhabited cays of La Cordillera Reserve — Icacos, Palomino, or Palominito. Open-bar catamaran with two snorkel stops on healthy reef, anchored beach time on a postcard sandbar, and a buffet lunch on board.
items.why_it_matters: The single best 'BVI-style' deserted-island day from San Juan — uninhabited, snorkel-grade reef, and no overnight or ferry required.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 1 hr drive E via PR-3 to Puerto del Rey, Fajardo; many operators offer hotel pickup
items.accessibility_notes: Catamaran boarding involves a steep gangway; not wheelchair accessible on most vessels. Sea swells common; bring motion-sickness meds.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit, reef-safe sunscreen, towel, hat, GoPro; snorkel gear + lunch + drinks included

items.name: Surfing Day Trip — Rincón (West Coast)
items.hours: Best surf Oct-Mar; lessons daily 8am-3pm by reservation. Domes/Maria's break.
items.admission_cost: $75-$120 group lesson (2 hr) / $150-$200 private; board rental $25-$35/day
items.description: Cross-island drive to Rincón, the surf capital of the Caribbean. Beginner lessons at sandy-bottom breaks like Sandy Beach, intermediate-to-advanced at Domes, Maria's, and Tres Palmas reef. Whale-watching off the point from January-March.
items.why_it_matters: The biggest, most consistent winter surf in the Caribbean — Rincón hosted the 1968 World Surfing Championship and remains a pilgrimage for surfers who want real waves, not metro shore-break.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 2.5-3 hr drive W via PR-22 (toll) — best done as overnight, but doable as a long day trip
items.accessibility_notes: Not wheelchair accessible. Beginner lessons require ability to swim. Long drive — consider overnighting in Rincón.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit, rash guard (lessons include), reef-safe sunscreen, towel; surf school provides board and leash

items.name: Wilderness Beach Surf & Crash Boat — Aguadilla
items.hours: Beaches sunrise to sunset; surf lessons 8am-2pm by reservation.
items.admission_cost: Free beach access; lessons $75-$110 group / $140-$180 private
items.description: Wilderness (aka Surfer's Beach) sits on the old Ramey Air Force Base bluffs with consistent reef-break waves and dramatic limestone cliffs. Crash Boat Beach nearby offers calm snorkeling and a sunset food-shack scene with fresh empanadillas.
items.why_it_matters: An easier-to-reach surf alternative to Rincón with a wilder, less-developed feel — and Crash Boat is the most photogenic sunset-bar beach on the west coast.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 2.25 hr drive NW via PR-22 to Aguadilla
items.accessibility_notes: Wilderness requires a short cliff descent on a dirt path — not accessible. Crash Boat is closer to flat-access friendly. Long drive; consider an overnight.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit, reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes (rocky entry at Wilderness), towel, cash for kiosks

items.name: Rappelling & Canyoneering at San Sebastián / Las Marías
items.hours: Tours by reservation only; typical 8am or 9am departure, Wed-Sun.
items.admission_cost: $135-$185 per person (full day, includes gear, lunch)
items.description: Strap into a harness and descend 60-100 ft waterfalls in the mountainous interior with licensed canyoneering guides. Routes include river-walking, swimming through pools, and 2-3 waterfall rappels, ending at a swimming hole. Beginner-friendly with full instruction.
items.why_it_matters: Puerto Rico's only proper waterfall-rappelling experience — a level of adventure most travelers don't even know is possible in the Caribbean.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 90 min drive W via PR-22 to San Sebastián; tour pickup often available from western hotels
items.accessibility_notes: Not accessible. Must be able to swim, comfortable with heights, and physically able to hike wet, uneven terrain. Minimum age typically 12; weight limits apply for harness fit.
items.gear_needed: Quick-dry clothes you don't mind ruining, water shoes or trail runners, change of clothes, dry bag for phone; technical gear (harness, helmet, ropes) provided

items.name: Parasailing — Isla Verde Beach
items.hours: Daily 10am-5pm, weather-dependent; check-in at hotel beach concessions.
items.description: Lift off from the back of a powerboat 400-600 ft above Isla Verde, taking in views from El Morro to El Yunque on a clear day. Wet or dry landing options; tandem rides are the most popular for couples and friends.
items.why_it_matters: The easiest aerial adventure from a San Juan hotel beach — no driving, no full-day commitment, and the only way to see the metro coastline from the air without a helicopter.
items.walkability_from_old_san_juan: 15 min Uber to Isla Verde; walkable from any Isla Verde hotel
items.accessibility_notes: Weight limits 100-450 lbs (tandem). Operators typically require ages 6+; under 18 with parent. Not wheelchair accessible boarding the boat.
items.gear_needed: Swimsuit (in case of wet landing), GoPro mount (provided by some operators), sunglasses with strap; PFD and harness provided
